summaryText:
In week seven of the Change series at Impact Church, Pastor Darrison Telles of Free House Miami brought a message titled The Challenge of Change. The service opened with a testimony from Taylor, who described how Jesus brought lasting change after years of hardship, addiction, and legal trouble. A short illustration of a caterpillar becoming a butterfly set the theme: God does not want to improve us a little, He wants to transform us completely. Pastor Darrison taught from 1 Peter 2, reminding believers that they are living stones, a chosen people, and God's special possession. He noted that Scripture itself says the road of life is narrow and not easy (Matthew 7). He then walked through three challenges that come with a changed life.

First, things get different. Jesus did not preach a better version of the old life but a completely different kingdom. Using a humorous illustration about a seat behind a pole, Pastor Darrison encouraged those in unfamiliar seasons to trust that God has prepared a place for them. Drawing on Galatians 2:20, he taught that we cannot be both the same and different. We die to ourselves daily, and the Holy Spirit, our Advocate, guides us in what to say, think, and do (John 14).

Second, things get difficult. Changed lives can mean letting go of old friendships, habits, dreams, and hurts, and the gospel can feel offensive. Using Mark 5, he observed that the people of the region were more unsettled by a restored man than by the man's former torment. He challenged the church to welcome God's work even when it is uncomfortable, and to delight in the difficult as Paul did in 2 Corinthians 12.

Third, we face doubt. Pastor Darrison shared, for the first time publicly, how he and his wife stepped out in faith to plant a church in Miami. He described taking an early-morning warehouse job at UPS, where he felt hidden and discouraged. Yet God used that season, and he found ways to share Jesus with coworkers who became friends. Turning to Mark 9, he highlighted the father who prayed, "I believe; help my unbelief," showing that faith and doubt can exist together and that God meets us honestly.

The message closed with an invitation to receive Jesus, a prayer of salvation, and prayer for those facing difficulty and doubt, with the encouragement that God shows up at the right time.
mainPoints: When God changes you, things become different: He offers not a better version of the old life but a new life, a new identity, and a new kingdom, as we die to self daily and rely on the Holy Spirit.

When God changes you, things can become difficult: the call to let go of old ways and the offense of the gospel can be uncomfortable, yet we can learn to delight in the difficult and welcome God's work.
When change takes time, doubt can creep in, but faith and doubt can coexist, so we can pray honestly, 'I believe, help my unbelief,' and trust that God shows up at the right time.

As you come to him, the living Stone, rejected by humans but chosen by God and precious to him, you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For in Scripture it says: 'See, I lay a stone in Zion, a chosen and precious cornerstone, and the one who trusts in him will never be put to shame.'

Now to you who believe, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe, 'The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,' and, 'A stone that causes people to stumble and a rock that makes them fall.' They stumble because they disobey the message, which is also what they were destined for.

But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession, that you may declare the praises of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light. Monday.scripture: 1 Peter 2:2 - "Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation."
Monday.focus: Healthy things change and grow. Crave God's Word as the source of real transformation.
Monday.action: Spend ten minutes reading 1 Peter 2:1-10. Write down one area where you sense God is inviting you to grow or change.
Monday.prayer: Lord, give me a hunger for Your Word. Change me from the inside out, and help me not settle for a slightly better version of my old self. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Galatians 2:20 - "I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me."
Tuesday.focus: God offers a new life, not just an improved one. We die to self daily so Christ can live in us.
Tuesday.action: Choose one habit, attitude, or priority you are holding onto. Write it on a card, pray over it, and ask God to replace it with His way.
Tuesday.prayer: Jesus, I surrender my own way today. Live in me and through me, and help me follow You daily. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: John 14:26 - "But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have said to you."
Wednesday.focus: When life feels different and unfamiliar, the Holy Spirit guides us in what to say, think, and do.
Wednesday.action: Before an important decision or conversation today, pause for one minute of quiet prayer and ask the Holy Spirit for wisdom. Then listen before you act.
Wednesday.prayer: Holy Spirit, I do not have all the answers, but You do. Teach me, remind me of Your truth, and lead me today. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 12:10 - "For Christ's sake, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong."
Thursday.focus: Change can be difficult, but God is present and at work in our hard seasons.
Thursday.action: Name one difficult thing you are facing. Thank God for one way He has been faithful in it, and send an encouraging message to someone else in a hard season.
Thursday.prayer: Father, help me trust You in the difficult. Be my strength where I feel weak, and show me how to keep following You. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Mark 9:24 - "I do believe; help me overcome my unbelief!"
Friday.focus: Faith and doubt can exist together. We can bring our honest questions to Jesus.
Friday.action: Write a short, honest prayer naming one doubt you carry. Beside it, list two ways God has shown up for you before. Share it with a trusted friend or small group leader if you are comfortable.
Friday.prayer: Lord, I believe, but help my unbelief. Strengthen my faith, and remind me that nothing is too hard for You. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: 1 Peter 2:9 - "But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession, that you may declare the praises of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light."
Saturday.focus: You are God's special possession, called to declare His praise through the story of how He is changing you.
Saturday.action: Share one way God has changed you, either with a friend or family member, or by emailing your story to your church. Invite someone to join you at church or to watch a message online.
Saturday.prayer: God, thank You for calling me out of darkness into Your light. Give me courage to share what You are doing in my life so others can know You too. Amen.

title: Why Real Change Feels So Hard | The Challenge of Change
